Converter based on maths-12-4's (Determinants, Hindi, same repo, more evolved than maths-12-3's own Hindi twin for this exact chapter) bracketed-matrix CSS-grid rendering, merged with physics-12-5-en's (most recently built, English medium) general fixes: the more evolved strip_redundant_enumeration with telescoped-enumeration handling and a decimal-point guard, the any_part_has_solution fallback (needed for q_3.42/q_3.11-style flat shared-solution-across-all-parts items), note/figure group-kind handling, non-breaking hyphen before a wrapped negative digit, and an i.e./e.g./etc./Fig. abbreviation guard in the sentence-splitter (added after catching ex_3.19's own conclusion mis-splitting "i.e." into two stray one-word lines - a real bug, fixed before finalizing). New in this chapter's own converter, found by grepping 06_simplify/chapter.simplified.en.md for every used backslash-command per step_9/PROMPT.md's own discipline: (1) \prime (260 occurrences, transpose notation) was entirely unhandled by BOTH inherited converters - added, the single most consequential fix here; (2) round-paren matrices (\left(\begin{array}...\right), 687 occurrences, actually the majority shape here vs. 377 square-bracket ones) were not detected at all by the inherited matrix-span finder (square-bracket-only) - extended to recognize both delimiter styles with visually distinct flank CSS (.s94/.s95/.s96 square, .s94p/.s95p/.s96p rounded); (3) \binom{a}{b} (8 occurrences, simultaneous-equation column-vector notation) - unhandled by both inherited converters, added a dedicated 2-row stacked renderer; (4) \mathbf (2 occurrences) and \pm (0 occurrences, added defensively) were missing from the Maths-lineage converter specifically. Also hardened the matrix/generic-array body finder to be nesting-depth-aware (same-name \begin/\end matching) rather than a naive first-match str.find, defensive against the ~13 places an outer plain array wraps sibling matrices as cells. Full command-coverage check (every \[a-zA-Z]+ token actually used in 06_simplify vs. the converter's own macro table) passed with zero gaps.
